newsitem.title: UK: SBC Warburg says EMU will boost corporate bond mkt.
newsitem.headline: SBC Warburg says EMU will boost corporate bond mkt.

text.p: European economic and monetary union (EMU) will boost the development of a European corporate bond market, a report by SBC Warburg said on Wednesday.

"As companies take advantage of the absence of foreign exchange risk and the reduction in yield, they may rely less on borrowing from banks and resort to greater bond issuance," the report, called "EMU - Opportunity of Threat?", said.

The European Union was likely to be rated triple-A and this would be the new ceiling for borrowers within the EMU zone, leading to improved credits for some companies now limited by sovereign ceilings, SBC Warburg said.
"Corporates of good credit quality in countries such as Italy could see their debt credit rating rise, making debt issuance potentially more attractive," the report said.
SBC Warburg expected there would be cost savings for corporates from the treasury function and from simplified operating methods although the cost of implementation was likely to be high.

"We believe that EMU offers excellent long-term opportunities but be prepared for a bumpy ride," Marc Hendriks, global head of macro economic research said in a statement giving details of the report.

SBC Warburg said it expected EMU in January 1999 to include Germany, France, the Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg, Austria, Ireland and Finland. By the end of July 1999, EMU would also include Italy, Spain, Portugal and Sweden, the statement said.
